labels.label: def:constants
labels.notes: I read perforated.tex l.311-330 in full (setting l.311-314, definition l.316-326, « Both are finite » l.328) and the ledger row (tex_span 316-326, lean_proved partial, blocked_on T-perf-poincare + OQ-109). The paper asserts four things: (a) λ₁ > 0, (b) λ₁ is the best Poincaré constant and equals the first non-zero Neumann eigenvalue, (c) C_SP is the least Sobolev-Poincaré constant, (d) both are finite. In Lean, with Star3's strict definitions, `0 < lambda1` means the set {λ > 0 | IsPoincareConst λ} is nonempty and bounded (sSup is 0 otherwise), so it covers (a) and the finiteness of λ₁. `isPoincareConst_lambda1` and `le_lambda1` give (b) without the eigenvalue form. `∃ C, IsSobolevPoincareConst C`, `isSobolevPoincareConst_Csp` and `Csp_le` give (c) and the finiteness of C_SP. `MeanPoincare` is the form the consumers carry. MODEL: `def_constants_of_analytic` concludes all of this from [IsFiniteMeasure vol], hD, SobolevIneq, RellichProp, ConstLimit (the repaired one, with MemLp f 2) and NonConst. These are jointly satisfiable (`toy_def_constants`, sorry-free). MANIFOLD: `Mfd.readingModel_def_constants` carries only setting hypotheses: 3 ≤ N (the paper's l.106 « Throughout, N ≥ 3 »), CompactSpace, T2Space, ConnectedSpace, a smooth manifold with boundary, a RiemannianMetric g, IsLocallyLebesgue μ, μ ≠ 0. Given IsLocallyLebesgue, μ ≠ 0 is equivalent to M nonempty (`measure_pos_of_isOpen`), and the paper's Σ is nonempty since ∂Σ ≠ ∅. It takes any σ, any n and n = 0, so ∂Σ ≠ ∅ is genuinely dropped (Lean ≥ paper there). Every analytic input is discharged by a sorry-free strict lemma: hD by Reads.hD, RellichProp by Reads.rellichProp, ConstLimit by Reads.constLimit, SobolevIneq by Reads.sobolevIneq, finite volume by isFiniteMeasure_of_isLocallyLebesgue, NonConst by readingModel_nonConst. Lean is narrower than the paper on three points, all disclosed in the docstring checklist, SCOPE and REPORT, under OQ-93 (a)(b) and OQ-109, which are open. (i) The metric and manifold are smooth, not Lipschitz. (ii) W^{1,2}(Σ) is C¹(M), so 0 < λ₁(C¹) and C_SP(C¹) < ∞ are weaker than the W^{1,2} statements until density is formalized. (iii) The eigenvalue form is not stated. The row is `partial` and unmarked, as the dispatch requires, so there is no faithfulness defect. NECESSITY OF THE EXTRA MODEL HYPOTHESES. (1) NonConst is necessary. `lambda1_eq_zero_of_forall_const` is conditional, so I checked a witness by probe: a one-point model with D = ℝ (constants only) and counting measure. It meets hD, ConstLimit and finite volume, and λ₁ = 0 there. RellichProp also holds there (finite-dimensional), though I did not formalize that. (2) hD is necessary, but the closer asserts this through kb 0023 and does not formalize it. I checked it mathematically: on [0,1] take D = ℝ², val(a,b) = a + b·1_B with B a Bernstein set, and d(a,b) = b. The inner-integral eLpNorm of a + b·1_B is min(|a|, |a+b|). This model satisfies RellichProp (limit f = lim a_k), ConstLimit (b_k → 0 forces a_k → f in L²), finite volume and NonConst. But MemLp fails, so MeanPoincare fails, and the junk mean 0 gives λ₁ = 0 (take a = 1, b = ε). So the claim is true. (3) Finite volume is NOT necessary: it follows from hD and RellichProp (finding 1). readingModel_nonConst is right. Two distinct points come from IsLocallyLebesgue with μ ≠ 0, since Lebesgue measure on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) has no atoms and N ≠ 0. A smooth Urysohn function, 0 near x and 1 near y, is then not μ-a.e. constant, because open nonempty sets have positive μ. The statement is the needed one and its hypotheses are satisfiable. toyCut_lambda1_eq_zero is correct: e = 1_true has zero energy and is not a.e. constant, so no λ > 0 is a Poincaré constant. The strict `toyCut_not_constLimit` shows ConstLimit fails on toyCut, and its RellichProp holds (finite-dimensional, not formalized), so the claim that connectedness is necessary stands. FINDINGS ABOUT THE PAPER: « no error » is right. The remark that l.319-320's « equivalently » needs connectedness is correct: on a disconnected compact Σ the first non-zero Neumann eigenvalue is positive, while a locally constant function with mean 0 gives a best Poincaré constant of 0. The wording of findings[0] needs a qualification (finding 2).

contradiction_argument: Read line by line (meanPoincare_of_rellich, l.128-233). The argument is genuine: it is lem:positivity's route and has no shortcut. If ν = 0, K = 0 works. Otherwise, by contradiction, for each k there is v_k with (k+1)·E(v_k) < a_k := ‖v_k − v̄_k‖²₂, and a_k > 0. Put w_k = a_k^{-1/2}(v_k − v̄_k·1). Then ‖w_k‖₂ = 1. E(w_k) < 1/(k+1), using d one = 0 (dirichlet_sub_smul_one). ∫w_k = 0, from integrability through memLp_two_of_rellich and finite ν. So w12Sq(w_k) ≤ 2 and RellichProp gives φ and f ∈ L² with ‖w_φk − f‖₂ → 0. Next E(w_φk) → 0, and ConstLimit applied to the subsequence gives f = c₀ a.e. ∫w_φk → ∫f through |∫(w − f)| ≤ V^{1/2}‖w − f‖₂ (Capacity's abs_integral_le_mul_eLpNorm_two), so V·c₀ = 0 and c₀ = 0. Then ‖w_φk − f‖₂ = ‖w_φk‖₂ = 1, which contradicts the limit 0. ConstLimit is used in its repaired form (MemLp f 2 is supplied by RellichProp).

The paper's sentences l.311-313 (truncated with [...]), l.319-324 and l.328 are quoted verbatim in > blocks. There is a ## Hypothesis checklist, a ## SCOPE (disclosed) and the Provenance line. findings.where: Poincare.lean:128, :341, :386 ([IsFiniteMeasure (M.vol g)] on meanPoincare_of_rellich, lambda1_pos_of_rellich, def_constants_of_analytic); docstring checklist l.58; REPORT notes and kb_proposals[0]
findings.what: The finite-volume binder is redundant. Applied to M.one, memLp_two_of_rellich hD hR gives MemLp (fun _ => 1) 2 (M.vol g), and memLp_const_iff then gives (M.vol g) univ < ∞. A probe confirmed this: an `example` derives IsFiniteMeasure and then MeanPoincare from hD, RellichProp and ConstLimit alone. The REPORT's « MeanPoincare needs hD and a finite vol besides them » is therefore inaccurate. The checklist's « Σ compact: carried as IsFiniteMeasure (vol g) and RellichProp » overstates what is carried. Faithfulness is not affected: the binder is implied by the paper's compactness, it is satisfiable, and it is discharged on the manifold.
findings.fix: Either drop the binder and derive it inside, from memLp_two_of_rellich at M.one and memLp_const_iff. Or keep it and correct the REPORT notes, kb proposal and checklist: finite volume follows from hD and RellichProp, and only hD and NonConst are needed beyond RellichProp and ConstLimit.

findings.what: « λ₁ > 0 and C_SP < ∞ hold under the standing hypotheses of l.311, as l.328 says » goes to the author as a fact. The Lean proves it only under the open readings of OQ-93 (a)(b): a smooth manifold and metric rather than Lipschitz, any locally-Lebesgue μ, and C¹(M) for W^{1,2}(Σ). Under (b) both conclusions are weaker than printed (λ₁(C¹) ≥ λ₁(W^{1,2}), C_SP(C¹) ≤ C_SP(W^{1,2})) until density is formalized. The sentence is mathematically true, but as written it reads as certified.
findings.fix: Qualify it: « … hold under l.311's hypotheses in the readings of OQ-93 (a)(b), proved for C¹(M) on a smooth compact connected manifold with boundary (Mfd.readingModel_def_constants); the W^{1,2} and Lipschitz cases are argued by density, not formalized ».
